data.name: AddOnsLede
data.value: One optional add-on. SnapZap scans, finds duplicates, exports and deletes without it.

data.name: AddOnsHint
data.value: Drop a file in and press Check again — no restart needed.

data.name: ExplicitLede
data.value: How hard SnapZap looks, and how sure it has to be before it says a photo is explicit.

data.name: TiledCheckboxLabel
data.value: Also look closely, in nine overlapping pieces

data.name: TiledCheckboxDetail
data.value: The model only ever sees a small thumbnail of what it is given, so a person who takes up part of a wide photo can vanish before it looks. Ten times slower.

data.name: WholeFrameHint
data.value: Off, expect misses. On one test folder this found 17 of 41; with it on, 25.

data.name: TiledHint
data.value: Photos scored the quick way are re-scored next time you press Score NSFW — the two answers aren't comparable.

data.name: SensitivityHeading
data.value: How sure it has to be

data.name: BlurbCautious
data.value: Flags only what is unmistakable. Fewest false alarms, most missed.

data.name: BlurbEager
data.value: Flags more, and puts more borderline photos in front of you. Still avoids the level where ordinary photos of people start getting flagged.

data.name: BlurbCustom
data.value: Your own levels. The measured safe floor is 0.50 averaged over the pieces.

data.name: BlurbBalanced
data.value: Recommended. On the folders this was measured against: 25 of 41 explicit photos flagged, and none of 263 ordinary ones.

data.name: TileMeanFlagLabel
data.value: Explicit, averaged over the nine pieces

data.name: SafeFloorWarning
data.value: Below {0:F2} this starts flagging ordinary photographs of people: one close-up of a face is mostly skin, and the model reads skin. Measured on a 17-photo family album — none flagged at {0:F2}, six at 0.40.

data.name: UnsureHint
data.value: The Not sure band is a queue for you to read. Set it low and it fills with photographs of faces — the model gives an ordinary portrait about 0.40 on skin tone alone.

data.name: LevelsApplyHint
data.value: Levels apply immediately to photos already scored — nothing is re-scored, only re-judged.

data.name: IdenticalFilesDetail
data.value: Byte-for-byte copies, by checksum. Always on — free and exact.

data.name: VariantLabel
data.value: The same shot at another size

data.name: VariantDetail
data.value: Resized, re-saved or converted copies of one photo. Safe to bulk-select.

data.name: VariantBitsHint
data.value: Lower is stricter. Raising it finds more, and eventually starts calling two different photos the same one.

data.name: BurstLabel
data.value: Bursts — the same scene, seconds apart

data.name: BurstDetail
data.value: Always detected. These are different photographs, so they are grouped for review and never picked up by "Select duplicate extras".

data.name: BurstWindowHint
data.value: Needs an EXIF capture time — photos without one are skipped, so a burst with no timestamps is not protected from bulk selection.

data.name: SettingsSavedHint
data.value: Saved. Run Find duplicates again to apply it.

data.name: CatalogueLede
data.value: What SnapZap remembers about the photos it has looked at.

data.name: ConfirmForgetBody
data.value: Discard the analysis of all {0} photos and {1} of thumbnails?

data.name: ForgetHint
data.value: No photo is deleted or moved — only hashes, scores, dates and thumbnails, all of which a scan rebuilds. Anything already in the Recycle Bin stays restorable from History.

data.name: NsfwDepUnlocks
data.value: Scores every photo so you can filter explicit images.
